note: Hand-written with the help of an AI coding assistant (Claude) and reviewed by the author. texts: one background post per group, month of year and year covered; replies: comment pool used without repeats; descriptions: past events by group and local start date.

10: Book fair volunteers: the sign-up is on the office door.
Halloween parade is the 31st at 9. Costumes should be easy to walk in, no masks that cover the eyes.
11: Our class is short two chaperones for the museum trip.
Conference slots open Monday at noon. The evening ones go fast.
12: Please label lunch boxes, we have five identical blue ones.
Winter concert is Thursday at 6:30. Second graders wear something red or green if they have it.
01: The art room is collecting egg cartons and corks.
Indoor recess all week with this cold. Our room could use a few board games if anyone is clearing out.
02: Lost and found is overflowing again. Everything unclaimed goes to donation on Friday.
Valentine class lists came home in folders. Please do a card for every kid so nobody is left out.
Snow day makeup is now the Monday after spring break, per the district calendar.
03: Thanks to everyone who sent snacks for the field trip.
Science fair projects are due the 20th. Trifold boards are at the front office for a dollar.
04: The rec center spring break camp still has spots for ages 6 to 10.
05: Does anyone have a spare recorder for the music unit?
Teacher appreciation week starts Monday. Our class is doing handwritten notes on Tuesday.
06: Thank you for a great year, everyone.
Last day is a half day, pickup at 12:15.
07: The school garden needs watering helpers over the break.
anyone know when the supply lists for next year get posted?
08: Carpool from Elm Ave has two open seats on Thursdays.
Kindergarten orientation is the 27th. New families, the playground stays open after so the kids can meet.
09: Picture day forms are due Monday.
First PTA meeting is Tuesday at 7 in the library. Free babysitting in the art room.

10: Free tomato cages by the gate.
Pull your tomato plants before the first frost. Bag the blighted ones, they do not go in the compost.
11: Mulch delivery is coming Saturday morning.
Spigots get shut off on the 15th. Drain and coil your hoses before then.
12: Garlic is in. See you in spring.
Quiet month out there. If you walk past, check the shed door is latched, the wind keeps pulling it open.
01: Tool shed code changes on the first of the month.
A few of us are meeting at the library Saturday to plan seed orders together. Bring your wish lists.
02: The trowel someone left by plot 6 last fall is in the shed now, on the hook by the door.
Plot renewals are due by the end of the month. Two plots are opening up for the waitlist.
Started peppers under lights at home. I will have extras to share in May.
03: Compost bins 2 and 3 are ready to turn.
Peas can go in once the soil is workable. The north beds are still too wet to dig.
04: Water is back on at the north spigot.
Frost warning tonight, cover the lettuce. Old sheets are in the shed.
05: The bees are out, mind the hive corner.
Hold off on tomatoes until after Memorial Day weekend. We have lost starts to a late cold snap before.
06: Aphids on the kale again. Soapy water works.
Summer watering schedule is posted on the shed. Please take at least one week in July.
07: The rain barrel overflowed, I moved the hose.
Zucchini overload. Leaving a crate by the gate, take as many as you want.
08: Pumpkins are going strong in plot 9.
The basil in the shared herb bed is starting to flower, pinch it back if you are passing by.
09: Please close the gate, the rabbits are back.
Fall cleanup list is up. Plots need to be cleared by November 1.

10: Please keep the hydrant clear when parking.
Halloween reminder: porch light on means you are handing out candy. We ran out by 7 last year, stock up.
11: Leaf bags are at the corner for anyone who needs them.
City leaf pickup for our side is the week of the 17th. Piles at the curb, not in the gutter please.
12: The city tree crew is pruning the maples next week.
Holiday lights walk Sunday after dark. Meet at the corner of Maple St and Elm Ave, we will loop both blocks.
01: Snow shovels are in the shared bin by the lot.
The plow buried the end of every driveway at 5am. Anyone free to help the older folks on the 200 block dig out?
02: The streetlight at the corner is out, I reported it.
Pothole in front of 52 Maple is getting deep. It is reported, but drive slow until it is patched.
Dues are $20 per household this year. Drop an envelope in the treasurer's mailbox when you can.
03: Package left at 14 Maple by mistake, come grab it.
Clocks change this weekend. Good time to swap the smoke detector batteries too.
04: Street sweeping moved to Thursday this month.
Block yard sale is the first Saturday in May. Add your house number to the sign-up if you want to be on the map.
05: Free bookshelf on the curb at 31 Maple.
A gray cat with white paws has been napping on our porch all week. Very friendly. Is it yours?
06: Lovely block party, thank you all.
Block party planning on our stoop Wednesday at 7. Bring a chair and any ideas for the kids' games.
07: Recycling pickup is a day late this week.
Fireworks went until almost midnight. If your dog is missing, one was running loose near the corner this morning.
08: Who has a ladder I could borrow Saturday?
Water main work on the 100 block starts Monday. No parking on the odd side from 7 to 4.
09: Watch for the new speed bump near the school.
School drop-off traffic is heavy around 8. Please do not block driveways while you wait.

10: Who is in for the turkey trot?
Mornings are dark now. Wear a headlamp or something reflective for the 6am group.
11: Shoe swap at the next meetup.
Going to bib pickup for the turkey trot Wednesday night. Tell me by Tuesday and I will grab yours.
12: Ice on the north loop, take the river path.
Holiday lights run Thursday at 6:30. Slow pace, about 3 miles through the neighborhood.
01: Welcome to the new runners this month.
Snow on the loop. Tuesday run is canceled, back on Thursday if the paths are plowed.
02: Lost a glove near the bridge, black with a reflective strip.
Anyone training for a spring half? Thinking of a Saturday long run group around a 10 minute pace.
Heads up, the boathouse restrooms stay locked until March.
03: Track is closed Tuesday for the school meet.
Evening runs are light again with the time change. 6pm start from the boathouse.
04: The park opens the east gate at 6 now.
A few of us are doing the 10K on the 26th. Carpool leaves from the boathouse at 7.
05: Adding optional strides after the Wednesday run, about ten minutes. Totally fine to skip.
06: New route posted for the long run.
Heat advisory Saturday. Start moves to 6:30 and we are cutting it to 4 miles.
07: Easy 5 miles Sunday at 8, meet at the boathouse.
The water fountain by the bridge works again, finally.
08: Deer on the north trail this morning, two of them. Slow down around the bend.
09: Hydration stop at mile 3 is back.
Fall race calendar is pinned. Add the ones you are running so we can come cheer.

descriptions.g-parents|2025-02-08: We need help hanging banners and setting up the game booths before the carnival. Wear sneakers for the gym floor. The PTA is bringing coffee and bagels.
descriptions.g-runclub|2025-03-01: First club 5K of the year, untimed, one loop of the park and back to the boathouse. You can bring one friend. The lot fills by 7:45, so street parking on Elm Ave is your backup.
descriptions.g-garden|2025-03-22: Turning compost into the raised beds and fixing the two broken frames on the east side. Bring gloves and a shovel if you have one, we have a few to lend. If it rains we move to Sunday at the same time.
descriptions.g-block|2025-04-12: Meet at the Elm Ave lot to pick up bags, grabbers and vests. Teams split between the 100 and 200 blocks and we should wrap by noon. Older kids are welcome with a grown-up.
descriptions.g-garden|2025-05-03: Seedlings from our own beds: tomatoes, peppers, herbs and perennials divided from the front border. Most pots are $2 to $5 and cash helps. Money raised goes toward the water bill.
descriptions.g-parents|2025-05-17: Bring a blanket and a dish to share. The PTA covers drinks and paper goods, and grandparents and siblings are welcome, up to three guests per family. If it storms we move into the school gym.
descriptions.g-runclub|2025-06-07: Members only tonight, the school asked us to keep the list tight. Easy 400s and 800s by pace group, no spikes on this surface. Use the side gate on Maple St.
descriptions.g-block|2025-06-21: The street closes from 1 to 9. Grills at the north end, chalk and kids' games at the south end. Bring a side or dessert and your own chair, and up to four guests per household is fine.
descriptions.g-garden|2025-07-19: Bring a few ripe tomatoes from your plot, labeled with the variety if you know it. We slice, vote on favorites and save seed from the winners. Bread and salt provided.
descriptions.g-parents|2025-09-06: A chance to meet teachers and other families before the first full week. Ice cream is free. Room parents will have volunteer sign-up sheets at a table by the front doors.
descriptions.g-runclub|2025-09-13: Six to eight repeats on the north hill, walking down to recover. Meet at the bench at the bottom, the warm-up jog leaves at 7:30 sharp. Members only.
descriptions.g-garden|2025-09-27: Bring seeds you saved this summer in labeled envelopes. Take what you can use even if you did not bring any, there is always plenty. Extra envelopes and pencils on the table.
descriptions.g-block|2025-10-18: Rakes out for the sidewalks, plus a few yards for neighbors who can't manage their own this year. The association has bags, bring a rake if you own one. Piles go to the curb for the city pickup.
descriptions.g-parents|2025-10-25: Costumes optional, nothing too scary for the little ones. Pumpkin decorating, cider and a cakewalk. Suggested donation is $5 per family for classroom supplies.
descriptions.g-parents|2025-12-13: Kids make ornaments and cards in the library meeting room, all materials provided. Dress for glitter. Space is tight, so two guests per family at most.
descriptions.g-runclub|2026-01-10: Three or five miles depending on how icy the paths are. Wear layers, gloves and a hat. Afterward we warm up in the boathouse with hot drinks, members only for this one.
descriptions.g-parents|2026-03-14: Pies, cookies, anything round. Drop off baked goods in the lobby by 8:30 with an ingredient card for allergies. Most items are $1, proceeds go to the math club.
descriptions.g-garden|2026-03-28: This year the focus is fresh woodchips on the paths between rows and fixing the gate hinge. Wheelbarrows are in the shed. Plot holders can bring one helper.
descriptions.g-runclub|2026-04-11: Two loops of the park plus the river path out and back. Pace groups at 9, 10 and 11 minutes per mile, nobody gets left behind. Water table at the boathouse at the halfway point.
descriptions.g-block|2026-04-18: Same plan as last spring, but we are adding the alley behind the 200 block. Gloves and bags supplied, bring your own water. Rain date is the following Saturday.
descriptions.g-parents|2026-06-13: Volunteers run the stations: sack race, water relay and tug of war. Expect to get wet. Check in at the table by the field gate to get your station.
descriptions.g-garden|2026-06-20: Longest day of the year, so we eat in the garden until it gets dark. Bring a dish made with something you grew if you can, plus your own plate. Bug spray recommended.
descriptions.g-block|2026-06-27: This year the bounce house goes in the middle of the block, away from the grills. Please sign up for a shift at the drinks table. The street is closed to cars until 9.
descriptions.g-runclub|2026-08-15: Meet at the river path entrance on Elm Ave for an easy 4 miles as the sun comes up. Members only. Carry water, the fountains along the path are not always on.
descriptions.g-garden|2026-09-26: Our second swap. We are also collecting flower seeds for the school garden, so bring any extras. There will be a sorting table for beans, squash and greens.
descriptions.g-block|2026-10-17: Planting daffodils and tulips along the Maple St median for spring. Dues cover the bulbs, so bring a hand trowel and a kneeling pad. Please park on the side streets.
descriptions.g-parents|2026-10-24: Back in the gym with a costume parade at 4:30 and a chili table run by fifth grade families. Instead of a fee, bring a canned item for the food pantry drive.
descriptions.g-garden|2026-11-07: We break apart heads from last year's harvest, plant the cloves in the shared bed and mulch with straw. Takes about two hours.
descriptions.g-runclub|2026-11-14: Dress rehearsal for the trot: same 5K distance at a steady pace. Members only. We will sort out carpools for race morning after.
descriptions.g-block|2027-01-23: Yearly meeting for the 100 and 200 blocks. On the agenda: dues, the block party date and the speed bump request. Members only, and one person per household is plenty.
